sources: Decompiled jar source (Vineflower) and jar data/lang
Live configs: <game folder>/config/dragonminez (skills, techniques, training, combat, general-server, raids/, tournaments/)
World definition files: <game folder>/saves/New World/dragonminez (sagas/, quests/, sidequests/, npcs/, wishes/) – quest text from en_us.json
conventions: Live config values are used over jar defaults. Skills that exist only because the Noea add-on (or another add-on) wrote them into skills.json are left out: hakai, frostgodforms, godkienhancement, createdforms, pureprogress, divinerose, demigraforms, mimicforms, piccolobiodata, demonforms, sphinxianforms, alienforms, friezabiodata, superdash, flowstate, stepvanish.
'Ki Damage' / 'Strike Damage' are the player's derived damage values (from PWR / STR+SKP, see the stats page). Ticks: 20 per second.
Technique TP prices live in skills.json and are listed on each technique; the skills array holds the non-technique skills (movement, utility, power, form groups).

tpSources.name: Quest / raid / tournament / wish rewards
tpSources.baseTp: Flat amounts set by each quest, raid, tournament or wish. Quest 'attribute' rewards pay half as Attribute Points and the rest as the TP those points would cost you now (attributeRewardPointRatio 0.5).
tpSources.notes: Boosts: class, racialskill, htc, otherworld, gravity, weights, global, potion, mutant, difficulty (only STORY gets the difficulty multiplier). TP from quests can be shared with party/fusion partners (partyTpShareRatio 0.5).

tpRules: TP buys one stat point at a time. Cost of the next point: cost = max(minTPCost, floor((minTPCost + V(S)) × globalTPCostMultiplier × class tpCostMultiplier) − max(0, maxTPDiscount − S)), where S = sum of your six stats (STR, SKP, RES, VIT, PWR, ENE) not counting points earned by Dynamic Growth practice (growthStatsCountForTpCost = false). Live values: minTPCost 16, maxTPDiscount 140, globalTPCostMultiplier 1.

V(S) (the growing part): with knee K = 5% of the max total stats (6 × maxValue 1,000,000 = 6,000,000, so K = 300,000): V = 1.25 × S below the knee; above it V = 1.25K + (1.25K / 0.7) × ((S/K)^0.7 − 1), i.e. cost keeps growing but more slowly.
The early-game discount (maxTPDiscount 140) knocks (140 − S) TP off while S < 140; the cost can never drop below minTPCost 16. dynamicGrowth.attributeTpCostMultiplier (1) only applies when above 1.

Class/race multiplier: each race's class block in the race stats config has tpCostMultiplier (and tpGainMultiplier); see the races page. Example costs with class multiplier 1.0: 60 total stats → 16 TP; 140 total stats → 191 TP; 500 total stats → 641 TP; 5,000 total stats → 6,266 TP; 50,000 total stats → 62,516 TP; 300,000 total stats → 375,016 TP; 1,000,000 total stats → 1,083,668 TP; 3,000,000 total stats → 2,524,233 TP; 6,000,000 total stats → 4,200,985 TP.
Buying many points at once just repeats the formula point by point (the cost is recalculated after each point). Manual TP purchases are enabled (dynamicGrowth.manualTpPurchasesEnabled).

TP gain multipliers are added, not multiplied: total = 1 + Σ(each boost − 1). Boost sources: class tpGainMultiplier; Frost Demon racial ×1.25; Hyperbolic Time Chamber ×1.75; being dead in Otherworld ×2; gravity training (+0.025 per point of net gravity); weights (×1–2.5, peak ×2 at the ideal load); global tpGainMultiplier ×1; potions/effects (TP Multiplier effect, Hero of the World effect, Kami's Blessing ×1.2); Mutant ×1.25; story difficulty (STORY only).

Progression catch-up: every source except TRAINING also gets + increaseTPGainRelativeToTPCost × sqrt(min(1, current stat cost ÷ cost at level 10,000)) = up to +75% as your stat costs rise (progressionReferenceLevel 10000).
Level is derived from stats: level = 1 + floor((S − starting stats) ÷ (6 × maxValue − starting stats) × (maxValue − 1)), so it is roughly your average stat. maxValue (per-stat cap) = 1,000,000.

Dynamic Growth is ON: stats also rise slowly by practising them (practiceXpMultiplier 2; per-stat multipliers STR 1, SKP 1, RES 1.5, VIT 0.5, PWR 1, ENE 1.5); farming the same target is reduced after 8 hits (×0.5) and 24 hits (×0.15) within 30 s. Details belong on the stats page.
Skills and techniques are bought with TP too (see skills/techniques); stat capsules give stat points directly (5 per normal capsule).

techniqueRules: Learning a technique skill (paying its TP at a master) unlocks the technique; equip it into one of 8 slots (Alt+1–4 = bar 1, Ctrl+1–4 = bar 2) from the Skills tab.

Techniques level up with use: +1 technique XP per hit and +3 per kill (per type in techniques.json; strikes 1/3, evasions 2 per hit). Upgrade cost starts at minXPCost 100 + 10 × the technique's complexity, × xpCostMultiplier 1 (no cap: maxXPCost -1). Humans gain 35% more technique XP (racial).

Ki upgrades: damage +0.05 multiplier, size +0.1, speed +0.05, armor penetration +1, cooldown −2.5% (to 50%), cast time; strike upgrades: damage +2.5% (max +50%) and cooldown; evasion upgrades: duration +2.5% (max +50%) and cooldown.

Ki technique cost formula: max(5, (0.5 × Ki Damage (without form multipliers) × damage multiplier + 5×size + 5×speed + 0.2×armor pen) × type factor × kiCostMultiplier × overload ÷ 2). Type factors: small ball 1.0, medium ball 1.4, giant ball 2.2, wave 1.6, laser 0.8, beam 1.4, disk 1.2, explosion 2.6, shield 1.6, barrage 1.4, area 1.8. Giant balls/explosions with damage > 2 pay an overload of min(3, 1 + 2×(damage − 2)). Heal-utility techniques cost ×1.25 and output 40%.

Cast times (ticks) from techniques.json: small_ball 0, medium_ball 30, giant_ball 60, wave 50, laser 0, beam 50, disk 30, explosion 60, shield 40, barrage 40, area 40. Small balls and lasers are instant.
Players can also design custom ki techniques in the technique editor (type, size, speed, colours, damage within per-type limits, optional buff/debuff); up to 256 unlocked techniques.

Play a song from a music disc you carry (requireDiscInInventory true; finish it with ≥75% accuracy to keep it without the disc) or Free Training (generated beat, 110 BPM +5/level up to 160). dimensions.name: Otherworld
dimensions.howToGetThere: Die (otherworldActive = true): you arrive as a spirit with a halo. Living players: Saiyan Space Pod destination (Otherworld enabled in config and after side quest "Otherworld Drive"), lands at 54, 210, 1082.

dimensions.name: Hyperbolic Time Chamber
dimensions.howToGetThere: Right-click the Time Chamber Portal block (at Kami's Lookout) – it toggles between Earth and the Chamber; or Saiyan Space Pod destination (after side quest "Temporal Comm-Link"), lands at 0.5, 130, 0.5.
dimensions.notes: TP ×1.75; Baba borrowed-time drains ×5; Mr. Popo inside offers rhythm training. Height only 96 blocks, coordinate_scale 100. Its gravity doesn't count toward the gravity-training TP bonus.

dimensions.name: Sacred Kai Planet
dimensions.howToGetThere: Saiyan Space Pod destination (after Buu Saga #23)
dimensions.notes: Sacred Kai plains/hills/rivers; Old Kai's pillar (Ultimate challenge). Reached in the Buu saga.

dimensions.name: Demon Realm
dimensions.howToGetThere: Saiyan Space Pod destination (after Daima Saga #3), lands at 160.5, 745, 0.5
dimensions.notes: Three stacked layers (First/Second/Third Demon World biomes), height 832. Demon villages, Gomah's soldier camps (raid), Gomah's Horn Cradle and the three Tamagami (world bosses), Demon Realm dragon balls (3) and Porunga (Daima). Daima saga.

dimensions.howToGetThere: Saiyan Space Pod destination (never unlocked by default)

worldBossRules: Group fights: contribution within 150 blocks counts (damage dealt, damage mitigated, damage received and healing, weights 1/1/1/1); minimum share to qualify 7.5%; top-3 ranks get +25%/15%/10% to drop chances.
Everyone has 3 lives; knocked-out teammates can be revived (15 s cast within 6 blocks, restores 25%, cooldown 90 s).
The boss gets +50% health and +25% damage per extra participant.

Lairs are structures (filled-map names exist for the Big Gete Star, Tamagami 1–3 and Gomah's Horn Cradle); the Hell Ogre in Otherworld points you to Janemba once his lair is known. Admin: /dmzworldboss locate|tp|reset|ready.

dragonBalls.how: Each set's balls generate as blocks in their dimension (1 copy per star, dragonBallSets; within 1000 blocks, dbSpawnRange; generateDragonBalls true). A Dragon Radar shows them (150 / 300 block ranges). Gather all of a set, place them within 5 blocks of each other in the right dimension and right-click one to summon the dragon. The dragon waits 10 minutes (12,000 ticks); after the wish(es) the balls scatter again (pending balls appear when their chunk loads).

Namek Dragon Ball: 7 balls in Namek
Demon Realm Dragon Ball: 3 balls in Demon Realm – no natural spawn, dropped by the Tamagami world bosses
